paper_title: A Birthday Repetition Theorem and Complexity of Approximating Dense CSPs
statement: Can Lemma 27 be used to prove new approximation guarantees for other problems?
context: While we settle down the approximability of dense Max k-CSP up to a k polylog(ki) factor in the exponent, our work raises many interesting questions such as the two listed below: Can Lemma 27 be used to prove new approximation guarantees for other problems? Lemma 27 is a generic bound relating expectations of a function on two distributions based on their informational divergence. Thus, it may help yield new approximation guarantees for other correlation-based algorithms. What is the right dependency on ε and c in the birthday repetition theorem? It is likely that the dependency of ε and c in our birthday repetition is not tight. In particular, parallel repetition for general games only has 1/c factor in the exponent whereas our theorem has 1/c2 ; would it be possible to reduce the dependency to 1/c in birthday repetition? Similar question also applies to ε.
